exposure: indication of admission to the delivery room
cohort: The study included 238 multiparous women with a history of vaginal birth at 37-42 gestational weeks.
finding: Lower Bishop score, lower biophysical profile, smaller gestational period, and lower birth weight were associated with requiring a C-section, while older age and a longer time interval from previous birth were associated with not requiring a C-section.
mod_finding: Factors such as lower Bishop score, lower biophysical profile, smaller gestational period, and lower birth weight were associated with a Cesarean section, contrasting with older age and longer time from previous birth being associated with vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: Measured; lower birth weight was associated with C-section.
gest_age: 37-42 gestational weeks; a smaller gestational period was associated with C-section.
